title: OpenAI posted 722 AI-written math papers. Now someone has to check them.

say: OpenAI just put 722 math manuscripts on GitHub.
Every one came from an AI model the public can't use.

clips.headline: OpenAI Drops 722 AI Math Manuscripts on GitHub. Experts Must Now Verify Them.
OpenAI Releases 722 Math Manuscripts From an Unreleased AI Model
OpenAI Publishes 722 AI-Generated Math Manuscripts, Including Work Tied to the Riemann Hypothesis

say: The model was given about 4,000 problems.
It produced 722 manuscripts, grouped into 372 families of results.
Those are different units, so they don't add up to a success rate.
scenes.verdict: Different units. Not a success rate.

say: On average, each result took about three hours of ChatGPT Pro compute.
scenes.small: of ChatGPT Pro compute per result, on average

say: The claims are big: the four-dimensional Kakeya conjecture, and work touching the Riemann hypothesis and the Hodge conjecture.
But the Riemann result is a weaker version. It doesn't solve the famous problem.
scenes.note: A weaker version. Not a solution.

say: Many come with proofs checked by Lean, a proof assistant.
One count found 162 manuscripts with formalized main results. That's 22.4 percent.
scenes.small: of 722 manuscripts have formalized main results

say: And a machine-checked proof isn't automatically a meaningful one.
These are preprints, not peer-reviewed papers.
An independent group of mathematicians advised OpenAI, but it says that doesn't mean it endorsed the results.
It wants this work kept where no AI lab is in control.
scenes.small: The advisory group wants results kept in repositories no AI lab controls.
scenes.credit: AGMAI statements, via XenoSpectrum and Unite.AI

say: The proofs are public. The model isn't.
Now it's up to mathematicians to check the work.
Sources: Gadget Review, Unite.AI and XenoSpectrum.
